One of this poet's poems repeats "I think I made you up inside my head" in parentheses. In addition to "Mad Girl's Love Song," this poet wrote that "I rise with my red hair / And I eat men like air" in "Lady Lazarus", which appears in her collection Ariel. One poem by this author calls the title man "a bag full of God," states that "every woman adores a Fascist" and begins with "you do not do / any more, black shoe." In another work by this writer of "Daddy", the protagonist is a student at Smith College dating Buddy Willard before attempting suicide. Name this female American poet who created Esther Greenwood in The Bell Jar.

In one section of this work, the words "Homo, fuge!" appear branded on the protagonist's arm, and in another section the protagonist steals the Pope's dishes and cup before boxing his ears. Part of this work features Benvolio growing stag horns, while in another part Valdes and Cornelius discuss magic after being summoned by the protagonist's servant Wagner. Its protagonist desires a female whose face "burnt the topless towers of Ilium" and launched a thousand ships, Helen of Troy. The titular scholar converses with Mephistopheles and sells his soul to the devil in, what play by Christopher Marlowe?
The Tragical History of Doctor Faustus

This man examined Madame Bovary in his essay The Perpetual Orgy, and in one of this author's works Bonificia and Father Garcia are two characters brought to Don Anselmo's title structure. Santiago Zavala and Ambrosio meet by chance at a dog pound in Conversation at the Cathedral, and this author of The Green House wrote a novel about conflict between the military and Antonio Conselheiro's followers in The War of the End of the World. Another of his novels features radio soap opera writer Pedro Camacho and Lucho's sister-in-law who journalist Mario falls in love with. Name this author of Aunt Julia and the Scriptwriter.

In one section of this work water burns "green and blue and white", while in another section of this work a character is described as having "skin as white as leprosy" and who "thicks man's blood with cold." That woman, Life-in-Death, wins the title character's life in a game of dice, and "slimy things with legs did crawl" in this work in which the Wedding-Guest leaves "a sadder and a wiser man." More notably, the title character exclaims there is "water, water everywhere / nor any drop to drink" and brings bad luck by killing the animal that "made the breeze to blow", an Albatross. Identify this epic about a cursed sailor by Samuel Taylor Coleridge.
The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

In one section of this work, the White Bone Demon is defeated, and later in this work a monk sees his body float under a bridge. Its protagonist can "cloud-somersault", could perform seventy-two transformations, is born from a stone egg on a mountain, and wields a golden-banded fighting staff. That character, who was sealed in a mountain after failing to escape from the Buddha's palm, is given a headband by Guanyin for a voyage in which the protagonist, Pigsy, and Sandy help Tripitaka obtain sutras. Name this work centering around Sun Wukong, one of China's Four Great Classical Novels by Wu Cheng'en.

He wrote that "beauty is its own excuse for being" in "The Rhodora" and claimed that "the highest end of government is the culture of man" to argue against property rights. His reading of the Vedas can be seen in a work defining the title concept as "not a faculty, but a light", "The Over-Soul", and he discussed two failures of historical Christianity in his Divinity School Address. In one work, the speaker says "I am nothing; I see all" after using the metaphor of a "transparent eye-ball". Another of his essays decries conformity and "foolish consistency" and advises "Trust thyself". Name this transcendentalist philosopher and author of "Nature" and "Self-Reliance".

Early on in this story the protagonist imagines "chambers hung with Oriental tapestries" and imagines "delicate meals, gleaming silver" while her husband admires their Scotch broth. Its protagonist requests four hundred francs to buy a new dress, and lives in an apartment at the Rue des Martyrs. Henry James' story "Paste" is a reversal of this story, in which after the protagonist loses the title borrowed object at the Minister of Education's ball, she and her spouse work for ten years to repay Madame Forestier. Name this short story in which Mathilde Loisel does not realize the title object is fake, a work by Guy de Maupassant.

The narrator of this book states that the most popular character is an undertaker who hits a dog for causing a commotion. That event occurs at a funeral for Peter Wilks, whose savings are stolen by two characters claiming to come from England and France. In this book, Harney and Miss Sophia elope during a conflict between the Grangerfords and Shepherdsons. Before meeting the aforementioned Duke and Dauphin, the main characters are dismayed when a bout of fog causes them to pass Cairo and miss the entry to the Ohio River. Name this novel about the runaway slave Jim and a comrade of Tom Sawyer sailing down the Mississippi, a book by Mark Twain.

Stories such as "Ah, Woe Is Me" and "The Talisman" appear in this author's short story collection The Soft Voice of the Serpent. This author wrote a work in which Kim Capran renames herself Hillela, A Sport of Nature, and wrote of the black overseer Jacobus and white farm owner Mehring in The Conservationist. In one of her novels the title woman has an affair with Bernard Chabalier and comes to terms with her father Lionel's reputation, Rosa, while another work follows the Smales family after they flee to their title servant's village. Identify this South African author of The Burger's Daughter and July's People.

In one section of this work, Pischik returns money to the protagonist after learning that Englishmen have discovered clay on his land. The events of this work are prompted by one character's return from Paris following her son Grisha's death. Characters in this play include one who is offered a job at a bank but eats sweets and plays billiards, Gayev, and in this play Varya fears that Trofimov and Anya have fallen in love. At the end of Act Three, Lopakhin reveals that he has bought the estate where he and Madame Ranevsky grew up. Name this Anton Chekhov play whose title entity is eventually cut down.

This author wrote a lengthy poem about Don Silva's fiancee Fedalma in "The Spanish Gypsy," and in one of this author's novels the title Jew helps Gwendolen Harleth and becomes Mordecai's disciple. This author of Daniel Deronda wrote a novel in which Tom and Maggie Tulliver ultimately reconcile before drowning in a flood. In addition to The Mill on the Floss, she wrote a novel in which the title character marries Dinah Morris after Hetty Sorrel hangs, and another in which a Raveloe inhabitant cares for Eppie after Dunstan Cass steals his gold. Name this pseudonymous female author of Adam Bede and Silas Marner.

In one of this man's works, the titular ex-con man supports himself by selling refrigerators, while in another work Levee kills his bandmate Toledo after being fired by the title woman. In addition to King Hedley II and Ma Rainey's Black Bottom, this author wrote about Hammond Wilks' plans for building a high-rise apartment on Wylie Street in one work. Besides Radio Golf, more well-known plays by this man include one centering on garbage truck driver Troy Maxson and one in which Boy Willie wants to sell the titular object for Sutter's land, both appearing in this man's Pittsburgh Cycle. Name this American playwright of Fences and The Piano Lesson.

In two of his short stories, Meatball Mulligan throws a party and Bongo-Shaftsbury kills the spy Porpentine. Stories such as "Entropy" and "Under The Rose" appear in his short story collection Slow Learner, and in one of his works the story of two colonial men is told by Wicks Cherrycoke. In addition to Mason & Dixon, this man wrote a novel in which the secret society Tristero attracts the attention of Oedipa Maas, while his best-known work follows the promiscuous protagonist's quest for the secrets of the Schwarzgerat and the V2 rockets, lieutenant Tyrone Slothrop. Name this reclusive author of The Crying of Lot 49 and Gravity's Rainbow.

In one section of this work, Stetson is asked if a corpse planted in a garden has begun to sprout and whether it will bloom next year. In another episode the Smyrna merchant Mr. Eugenides asks the narrator out to lunch, and another section recounts the drowning of Phlebas the Phoenician. The phrase "HURRY UP PLEASE IT'S TIME" is repeated five times in capital letters, although better-known phrases from it include "London Bridge is falling down" and "Unreal City". It begins with an epigraph in which the Cumean Sibyl states "I want to die," which immediately precedes its opening line "April is the cruelest month." Tiresias narrates what poem by T. S. Eliot?

In one of his works, Extravagario, he reflects on his youth and political affiliations by presenting the reader with an analysis of his daily life. Another work by this man entitled Residence on Earth includes the poem "Hymn to Celery". In another work, he attempted to chronicle the history of the Spanish-speaking nations of Central and South America and included sections entitled "The Conquistadors", "The Fugitive", and "A Lamp on Earth". That work also contains a work based on a visit to the titular city, "The Heights of Macchu Picchu". Name this winner of the 1971 Nobel Prize in Literature, a Chilean poet who wrote Canto General and Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair.

One of this man's works tells the story of Hans Giebenrath, who chooses the life of a blacksmith over that of a scholar, in his novel Beneath the Wheel. He depicted episodes of Emil Sinclair's life in the Scheinwelt in Demian, while he portrayed the composer Kuhn's relationship with opera singer Heinrich Muoth and the title woman in Gertrude. This man wrote a novel in which the protagonist searches for enlightenment with his friend Govinda, while in his probably best-known work, the protagonist encounters the saxophonist Pablo through Hermine, and discovers the Magic Theatre. Name this German-Swiss author who wrote Siddhartha and created Harry Haller in Steppenwolf.

In one section of this work one character has a vision of Socrates wooing Phaedrus, and in another the protagonist sips pomegranate juice and soda water on a terrace. This novel's protagonist stays at the Hotel des Bains and is disgusted by seeing an old man wearing youthul makeup, though he wears such makeup later in this novel while eating overripe strawberries. The protagonist learns of a cholera epidemic in his city, but does not warn a character who visits the beach with his friend Jasiu; the protagonist dies in a chair there while watching that character, Tadzio. Name this novella featuring Gustav von Aschenbach, a work by Thomas Mann.

In one episode in this work a character proclaims that "God has arrived" as the blind pianist George Shearing enters the bar and performs, while in another the protagonist moves in with Roland Major. Characters in it include Galatea Dunkel, whose husband Ed keeps leaving her to travel, and Remi Boncoeur, who invites the protagonist to San Fransisco. The protagonist meets Mississippi Gene and Montana Slim on his way to Cheyenne, from where he hitchhikes to Larimer Street. Near the end of the novel, he catches dysentery in Mexico City and is left there by Dean Moriarty. Narrated by Sal Paradise, name this definitive work of the Beat Generation, a novel by Jack Kerouac.

In one episode in this novel, the protagonist cuts out a Kruschen Salts advertisement that amuses him and pastes it into an album. Minor characters in this novel include Thomas Perez, the protagonist's mother's friend, and Celeste, whose restaurant the protagonist frequents. The protagonist acts as a police witness for warehouse guard Raymond Sintès, despite his reputation as a pimp, and he's proposed to by Marie Cordona, who visits him in his jail cell after he's arrested for killing an Arab, although his trial concentrates on his lack of grief shown at a funeral. Meursault is the emotionless protagonist of what work of Albert Camus?

Ezra Pound's second Canto begins by telling this man to "hang it all", as "there can be but one 'Sordello!'" He wrote "Grow old along with me! The best is yet to be" in a poem appearing in his collection Dramatis Personae, and in addition to "Rabbi ben Ezra," he wrote a work in which the narrator used "one long yellow string" of his lover's hair to strangle her. This author of "Porphyria's Lover" more famously wrote a poem in which the narrator's "nine-hundred-years old name" was ranked "with anybody's gift" by a woman with "a heart too soon made glad" painted by Fra Pandolf. Name this English poet of dramatic monologues including "My Last Duchess."

One character in this novel speaks with Conte Altamira and Don Diego Bustos after discussing how to woo a woman with Prince Korsakoff, and in another episode from this novel a character memorizes a message for the duke of Angouleme. Characters from this novel include Chénal, who arranges for its protagonist to tutor the mayor of Verrieres' children, and Elisa, the chambermaid who exposes its protagonist's affair. Its protagonist is attracted to Mathilde de la Mole, and near the end of this work travels to his hometown to shoot Madame de Renal. Julian Sorel is the protagonist of what novel by Stendhal?

One character in this novel is worried after hearing an acquaintance dined with the Cox family at the Coles' party, and another character in it travels to Highbury as a result of Colonel and Mrs. Campbell's trip to Ireland. One episode in this novel sees boarding school mistress Mrs. Goddard attend a dinner party, and this novel begins with Miss Taylor leaving Hartfield. The niece of the chatty Miss Bates, Jane Fairfax, is secretly engaged to Frank Churchill in this novel, which later sees Robert Martin, rather than Mr. Elton, ends up marrying Harriet Smith. The titular matchmaking female eventually marries George Knightley in what novel by Jane Austen?

Although married to Lew, Eloise pines for the killed-in-action Walt in this writer's short story "Uncle Wiggity in Connecticut," and in another story by him Sybil talks about the title creatures to Muriel's husband Seymour who later shoots himself. This author of "A Perfect Day For Bananafish" wrote a work in which one of the title characters dates Lane Coutell while the other argues with his mother Bessie, and in addition to Franny and Zooey, he wrote a novel in which a character is expelled from Pencey, cares for his sister Phoebe, and refers to fake people as "phonies." identify this creator of the Glass family who created Holden Caulfield in The Catcher in the Rye.

In one episode in this work, Doris Kilman shops for petticoats with Elizabeth while bemoaning the fact that her only pleasure left in life is eating. In another episode in this novel, Dr. Holmes calls cowardly a character who threw himself out of a window after considering a bread knife, a gas fire, and razors as methods of suicide, Septimus Smith. The protagonist later remembers kissing Sally Seton, who smoked cigarettes on the floor, after her old flame Peter Walsh returns from India. Name this stream-of-consciousness novel in which Big Ben constantly chimes, a work by Virginia Woolf centering around Clarissa's dinner party.

In this novel, one hundred people are invited to the protagonist's wedding, but only ten attend. The novel's protagonist is killed with a scythe on the same day that one of his children is born, and the novel ends with a character insisting "I don't hate it!" in response to Shreve's question. The man who later kills the protagonist rides a mule without a saddle and yells through a window that Charles Bon has been shot. Bon is killed by his half-brother, Henry, who wants to keep Bon from marrying Judith and later dies in a fire set by Clytie at the protagonist's Hundred. Wash Jones kills Thomas Sutpen in what novel by William Faulkner?

One of this author's works is narrated by a fetus conceived on Twelth Night and born on Columbus Day, while in another Felipe Montero sees the titular girl transform into a 109-year-old woman. In addition to Christopher Unborn and Aura, this author split one work into three sections titled The Old, New, and Next World respectively; that work, centered around the construction of the Escorial, is Terra Nostra. He wrote of General Arroyo and imagined the circumstances of Ambrose Bierce's death in one novel, while in a more well-known work he depicted the titular tycoon on his deathbed. Name this Mexican author of The Old Gringo and The Death of Artemio Cruz.

At the beginning of this work Aunt Julle's hat is mistaken for Berte's, while in another section the protagonist exclaims she is burning Thea's child. One character is repeatedly referred to as having "vine-leaves in his hair"; that character later dies at Mademoiselle Diana's soiree. The protagonist recounts lying about wanting to live in Councilman Falk's villa to Judge Brack in this play. The protagonist's husband is alarmed when he learns he may lose a professorship to Ejlert Lovborg, who the protagonist drives to commit suicide after he loses his manuscript. She then shoots herself in the temple in, what Henrik Ibsen play?

In this work, a cousin of the protagonist is sent to breathe a poisonous fire of love into the mouth of a hospitable Tyrian. During war with the Rutulians, the gods decide not to intervene in that character's fight with Turnus. Aeolus releases the winds from a mountain to destroy the protagonists' fleet at the behest of Juno, and the author makes many references to Augustus, the commissioner of this epic. The main character is noted for carrying his father Anchises and his son Ascanius out of a burning Troy, and leaving his wife Creusa behind. Name this work in which Queen Dido commits suicide, an epic about the titular Trojan hero by Vergil.

In one of this author's works Gervaise and Coupeau are happily married before sliding into alcoholism, and in another the title character and Laurent kill Camille to marry but later commit suicide. In addition to L'Assommoir and Therese Raquin, he wrote about the title female who stars in La Blonde Venus and destroys men who pursue her in one novel, and in another of his works Etienne Lantier becomes the leader of a miners' strike. One of his letters was published in newspaper L'Aurore and attacked Felix Faure. Name this French writer who included "Nana" and "Germinal" in his Rougon-Macquart Cycle and who defended Dreyfus in J'Accuse.

In one section of this work the narrator takes a trowel out of his roquelaire to demonstrate he is a mason, and soon after he tells a friend his family motto is "Nemo me impune lacessit." The narrator points out nitre gleaming on cavern walls and offers to impose on Luchesi rather than his sick friend. The narrator ends his retelling with "In pace requiescat!" after stating that for half a century no mortal has found the bones of the acquaintance whom he lured to his vaults due to his proud wine connossieurship. After crying "For the love of God, Montresor!" Fortunato is buried alive in, what short story by Edgar Allan Poe?

The title object, which "springest on this grassy slope", has a "quick cool murmur" in this poet's The Fountain, and this man attacked Thomas Jefferson's presidency in his satire The Embargo. Another of his poems mentions "the plashy brink" and begins with the line "Whither, 'midst falling dew". That poem speaks of a "Power whose care" "guides through the boundless sky" the titular creature's "certain flight", and this poet orders the reader to "approach thy grave" and "lie down to pleasant dreams" in another poem whose title means "meditation upon death". Name this American poet of "To A Waterfowl" and "Thanatopsis."

In one episode in this novel, the protagonist chooses one of four St. Bernard puppies and realizes the others must die. At her party, Marie-Claude declares that the pendant worn by a guest is ugly shortly before her husband Franz admits he has been unfaithful and flies to Sicily, and in another section of this novel, the protagonist repeats "es muss sein" in his conversation with the hospital director. The protagonist has many casual liaisons with women, the most notable being his mirror-obsessed mistress Sabina, who is befriended by his wife Tereza and is later devastated when both die in a truck accident. Tomas is the protagonist of what novel by Milan Kundera?

One of these has eyes of metal and agate in a poem by Charles Baudelaire, and another thinks he is "dying, Egypt, dying" and "thankful, thankful, thankful" while drowning in a Natsume Soseki novel. Johnnie Walker eats their hearts while Satoru Nakata finds lost ones in Murakami's Kafka On The Shore, and Alex is attacked by these as he tries to steal a bust of Beethoven in Burgess's A Clockwork Orange. A huge talking one named Behemoth appears in Bulgakov's The Master and Margarita, while Maggie Pollick is referred to as one of these in a Tennessee Williams play. Give the name of this creature which, in the title of the aforementioned play, appears on a hot tin roof.

The intellectual Cross Damon is murdered in this man's novel The Outsider, and he wrote a story in which the title character watches a mob tar and feather his friend Bobo. That story, "Big Boy Leaves Home", appears in his short story collection Uncle Tom's Children. He wrote of taking a command to kill a kitten literally and his Mississippi upbringing amidst racial tensions. This author of Black Boy created characters like the communist Jan and lawyer Boris Max in a novel featuring a character who scares Vera with a rat and plans a robbery with Gus before killing Bessie and Mary Dalton, Bigger Thomas. Name this author of Native Son.

At the end of this work, the stepfather of the title character is drawn and quartered and thirty-one of his kinsmen, including Pinabel, are killed. King Marsile of Zaragoza plots the demise of the title character with Ganelon, and in response to an ambush by a force twenty times greater than his own, Oliver advises the titular character to blow his oliphant horn, although the effort causes his temples to burst. It ends with Gabriel commanding Charlemagne to embark on another war. Name this tale, based on the Battle of Roncevaux Pass, that centers on the titular paladin of Charlemagne, the oldest significant surviving work of French literature.

In one of this man's works two women meet in a restaurant on Christmas Eve and Mrs. X discovers Mrs. Y's affair with her husband. This author of The Stronger portrayed the conflict between Laura and the Captain in The Father, and he wrote a work in which Edgar and Alice live in a fortress on an island. In one of his novels Berns Salonger serves as a meeting-place for Arvind Falk and others. Besides The Dance of Death and The Red Room, this writer wrote a play in which the cook Kristin's fiancee, Jean, has power struggles with the title aristocratic female. Name this Swedish playwright and author of Miss Julie.

One character in this novel moves to Michigan after receiving a letter addressed to "Mrs., Mr., Miss, or Mr. And Mrs.", followed by her surname. In this book, Popinjay gets in trouble for taking too-copious notes when Clevinger "always didn't say you couldn't punish me". A man in this novel who yearns tragically for Mary is accused of stealing a plum tomato and being Washington Irving. At the end of this novel, the protagonist flees from a prostitute whom Nately loved. The titular concept is first cited as the reason that the protagonist must keep flying missions. Name this novel titled after an air force-related paradox, a work featuring Yossarian written by Joseph Heller.

In one section of this novel, the protagonist's little brother Abraham eavesdrops on their parents at the local inn Rolliver's, while in another the protagonist asks her true love to marry Liza-Lu after she dies. In this work, the protagonist befriends Izz, Retty, and Marian while she is a milkmaid at Talbothay's dairy. The protagonist is either seduced or raped by her supposed cousin, and bears a child, Sorrow, who soon dies; her seducer later asks her to marry him. After she reunites with the man who couldn't forgive her and fled to Brazil, Angel Clare, the protagonist kills Alec and is subsequently hanged. Name this novel by Thomas Hardy.

In one poem in this work, the narrator speaks of "the woman meanwhile, twisting like a snake / On hot coals," while another describes the titular location as a place where "kisses, languishing or joyous [...] adorn the nights". Those poems, "The Vampire's Metamorphoses" and "Lesbos," were among those banned for indecency upon its publication. Poems such as "To She Who Is Too Gay" and "The Jewels" appear in its first and longest section, Spleen and Ideal, and the last line from its Foreword, which mentions a "hypocrite lecteur," was used in T.S. Eliot's "The Waste Land." name this poetry collection by Charles Baudelaire.

In one section of this work, the narrator calls himself "politic, cautious, and meticulous" and in another he claims to have "seen the moment of [his] greatness flicker". The speaker says "there will be time to murder and create" and exclaims that he's not Prince Hamlet, while in another part of this poem he "grows old" and "shall wear the bottom of [his] trousers rolled". Other parts of this poem see the narrator wondering if he dares to eat a peach and yellow fog rubbing its back against window-panes. Name this poem in which women talking about Michelangelo enter and exit a room and the speaker questions "Do I dare disturb the universe?", a work by T. S. Eliot.
The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock

One of this man's works involves Patron, Guide, and the Church of the New Man, and in another of his novels Ma-chan cares for her mentally retarded musician brother Eeyore. In one of his novels the titular spirit's name was the only word the composer D's infant son spoke; those novels were Somersault, A Quiet Life, and Aghwee the Sky Monster. Many of his novels are influenced by his autistic son Hikari, such as a novel involving Bird and his son with a brain hernia, and in one of his novels a character hangs himself after sodomy involving a cucumber. Name this Japanese author who wrote about Mitsusaburo and Takashi's return to a village in The Silent Cry.

This story begins with a poem by Sir Walter Scott that explains "From whence comes Wensday" and then goes on to describe the Katskills as "perfect barometers". The titular character is described as "thrice blessed" with his nagging wife. He spends most of his time with a group, led by Nicholas Vedder, of "sages, philosophers, and other idle personages". Upon being hailed by a strange man while squirrel hunting, he meets a band of Dutch settlers playing ninepins and drinks from a flagon which induces a certain condition. Name this "Posthumous Writing of Diedrich Knickerbocker" in which the titular character sleeps for twenty years, a short story by Washington Irving.

Minor characters in this work include Prokofitch, a servant at the Marino estate, and Sitnikov, a dim friend of the protagonist. The protagonist is condescending towards proto-feminist Madame Kukshin in one part of this work, and in another section in this work is rejected after confessing his love to Anna Odintsova. Nikolai muses on the rift between younger and older generations in this novel, while later the protagonist flirts with Fenechka and must duel Pavel Kirsanov as a result, the refined uncle of his friend Arkady. Name this novel with the nihilistic protagonist Yevgeny Bazarov, a novel by Ivan Turgenev.

A dog who bites a well-respected man dies soon after in this man's poem "Elegy on the Death of a Mad Dog." He wrote the letters of fictional Chinese gentleman Lien Chi Altangi in The Citizen of the World, and in one of his poems the "loveliest village of the plain," Auburn, is depopulated. This author of "The Deserted Village" wrote a work in which a woman disguises herself as a barmaid to gain Charles Marlow's affections, and another in which Mr. Burchell is actually Sir William Thornhill. Name this creator of Kate Hardcastle and the Primrose family, writer of She Stoops To Conquer and The Vicar of Wakefield.

Deborah awakes from a 30-year sleeping sickness-induced coma in one of this man's works, and Rebecca and Devlin interact in another of his works. In addition to A Kind of Alaska and Ashes to Ashes, Hirst drunkenly believes Spooner is an ex-classmate in one of this author's works, and in one of his plays featuring Lush and Ms. Cutts, Gibbs supplants Roote as the asylum's director. Better-known than No Man's Land and The Hothouse is a play in which Aston invites the homeless Davies into his apartment, and in another of his plays hit-men Ben and Gus hide in a basement with the title appliance. Identify this English playwright of The Caretaker and The Dumbwaiter.

One of this author's works involves Mrs. Guy, Charlotte, and Arthur Prime, and in another work Charlotte Stant and Prince Amerigo shop for but do not buy the title object before beginning an affair. In addition to writing "Paste" and The Golden Bowl, this author wrote about Winterbourne's courtship of the titular girl in Daisy Miller. In a more well-known work, the protagonist is fond of Pansy but is unhappy married to her father Gilbert Osmond, and in another work Miles and Flora are aware of the ghosts of Peter Quint and Miss Jessel. Name this author of The Turn of the Screw who created Isabel Archer in Portrait of a Lady.

This man "walked on the banks of the tincan banana dock" and tells the title object that "You were never no locomotive" in his "Sunflower Sutra," and poems such as "Iron Horse" and "Wichita Vortex Sutra" appear in this writer's collection The Fall of America. He spied Garcia Lorca "by the watermelons" and called Walt Whitman a "childless, lonely old grubber" in his work "A Supermarket in California," and mourned his mother Naomi in his poem "Kaddish." His best-known poem mentions "angel-headed hipsters" and is dedicated to Carl Solomon. Name this Beat Generation poet who wrote "I saw the best minds of my generation destroyed by madness" in Howl.

One of this author's stories includes the crucifixion of Peachey Carnehan between two trees and the death of Dan Dravot, who died when a rope bridge was cut. In another of this author's works, Mr. Lurgan uses jewels and a copper tray to improve the title character's memory in Simla. In addition to Kim, this author created a "regimental bhisti" in his Barrack-Room Ballads, Gunga Din. Identify this author who explained "How the Leopard Got His Spots" in Just So Stories who wrote about Rikki-Tikki-Tavi and Mowgli in The Jungle Book.

This author wrote "there is neither East nor West, Border, nor Breed, nor Birth / When two strong men stand face to face, tho' they come from the ends of the earth!" in a poem asserting "East is East, and West is West, and never the twain shall meet." This author wrote a poem about a British soldier who tells a water-carrier "you're a better man than I am," as well as several stories about the tiger Shere Khan and the wolf-child Mowgli. Name this British author who wrote about India in "Gunga Din" and The Jungle Book.

One character in this work has returned from a vacation in Florida, though another character notes that his mind was not rested. The central character recalls getting a job offer from his brother Ben, though he refused due to the inspiration he received from Dave Singleman. One character steals a fountain pen from Bill Oliver, though he realizes that he is unhappy in the city and longs for life on a ranch. The discovery of a tube behind a fuse box alarms Linda, and the image of stockings disturbs the main character due to his guilt over an encounter with a woman and his son Biff in Boston. Name this play in which Willy Loman kills himself for insurance money by Arthur Miller.

Near the beginning of this work one character states that "No man shall say that I betrayed a brother", and in another section of this work Tiresias prophesies the death of another character's five children. Characters in this work include the protagonist's sister Ismene, who tries to confess to the protagonist's crime, and her fiancee Haemon, who commits suicide and triggers Eurydice's death. After burying Polynices against the king's wishes, the protagonist is condemned to death by Creon, and this play is the third in a trilogy featuring the protagonist's father at Colonus. Identify this work by Sophocles about Oedipus' daughter.

He wrote a short story concerning an engineer in the town of Iguape, Brazil, titled The Growing Stone, which, along with works like The Guest and The Artist at Work, appears in his short story collection. His first novel sees the murder of Zagreus while the protagonist of another of his works mentions how he stole part of the Ghent Altarpiece and discusses how he "needed to feel above". In one work by this author, the protagonist helps his friend Raymond break up with his Moorish girlfriend.
